title: Where the Saplings Joined the Older Song

features.name: the-two-tree-threshold
features.desc-on-touch: A doorway between saplings and ancients, framed by wood that looks young and old simultaneously. The threshold hums with the moment of joining. Roots touch here beneath the soil.

features.name: the-root-intertwining
features.desc-on-touch: Deep beneath sight, you sense the moment: young roots braiding with ancient ones. Not invasion. Recognition. The old trees stop singing alone. The saplings stop listening. They sing together.

features.name: the-summer-they-learned
features.desc-on-touch: A pool of clear water reflecting both canopy heights at once: young tips and ancient crowns, both real, both singing. The pool knows the exact moment when the teaching became mutual.

features.name: the-witness-ring
features.desc-on-touch: Concentric circles of growth-rings, each one marking a year when the saplings learned another verse. The newest ring is still soft. It will know its own sound by next growth.

features.name: the-standing-instruction
features.desc-on-touch: An arch of older wood, bent into a teaching posture. Young branches nestle against it. The arch says: this is how you stand. This is how you belong here. This is your note.

inscription: the morning the young roots found they were never singing alone

file.name: Sapling_Integration_Summer_Log.txt
file.note: Records from the summer the young trees learned the older song. By autumn, nobody remembers teaching. The song became generic as air. Status: germinating.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the clearing where saplings first spoke
narr: You kneel in the soft earth with her. She is placing a
sapling. 'Listen,' she says. You do. The old trees are
already singing—you hear it now, in the soil, through your
knees. She presses the small root down into the choir.
'It will learn,' she says. 'We learned. They learn.' A
single petal falls between you. Neither of you moves.
